method: An O-ring seals because its cross-section is flattened between the bottom of its groove and the mating surface, and the three figures that decide whether a gland works are all dimensional. The radial squeeze is the free cross-section minus the gland depth, reported in millimetres and as a percentage of the free cross-section; the installed stretch compares the groove bottom diameter with the free inside diameter, (D_groove − ID_free) / ID_free, and matters because a ring pulled over a larger diameter thins as it stretches, so a squeeze read on the free cord is optimistic once the stretch passes a few percent. The gland fill divides the ring's cross-section area π CS²/4 by the groove's cross-section area, depth × width, and is the share of the groove the ring occupies cold; the void that is left has to absorb thermal expansion and any fluid swell. A 24.99 mm ring with a 3.53 mm cord, stretched over a 26 mm groove bottom and sitting 2.9 mm deep in a 4.6 mm wide groove, therefore reads 0.63 mm of squeeze (17.8 %), 4.04 % of stretch and 73.4 % of fill. Parker's O-Ring Handbook (ORD 5700, §3.6 squeeze and §3.7 gland fill) puts the minimum squeeze for any cross-section at about 0.2 mm, the maximum recommended squeeze for a static seal at 30 % and for a dynamic seal at about 16 %, and asks for a gland fill between 60 % and 85 % with the optimum near 75 %, so that at least 10 % of the gland stays void; its §5.10 on stretch notes that more than a couple of percent reduces the squeeze diameter, so the page warns above 5 %. It also warns when the groove is narrower than the cord, because the ring then bulges over the side walls, and when the groove bottom is smaller than the free inside diameter, because the ring no longer grips. Inputs are bounded: free inside diameter 3 to 2000 mm, free cross-section 0.5 to 25 mm, groove bottom diameter 3 to 2400 mm, gland depth 0.2 to 15 mm and groove width 0.3 to 60 mm, and a gland deeper than the free cross-section is refused because the ring would not be compressed at all. These are the handbook's dimensional rules only: the page does not model the diametral clearance the ring may be extruded into, the surface finish of the sealing faces, the pressure, temperature or the compound and its swell in the fluid, nor the backup rings a high-pressure gland needs, so it is a fit check rather than a seal design. Everything runs locally in the browser.
